f.title: MAHs selling drugs are responsible for post-market PV and GVP; selling under a name you control makes you a manufacturer
f.statement: Manufacturers or market authorization holders (MAHs) who sell drugs are responsible for post-market pharmacovigilance activities and good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP). When you sell a drug under a name you control, you meet the definition of a manufacturer.

rows.quote: Manufacturers or market authorization holders (MAH) who sell drugs are responsible for post-market pharmacovigilance activities and GVP. When you sell a drug under a name you control, you meet the definition of a manufacturer.
rows.review_note: Review: new row. The source makes selling MAHs responsible for post-market PV and GVP, and defines who is a manufacturer (who must report). The extractor missed it. Double-check: removed 'and carry these responsibilities' from the statement (not in the quote), and cleared legal_basis 'Food and Drugs Act s. 9': the quote does not cite it, and section 9 is mentioned in an earlier sentence for a different point. Below 90: 'are responsible for' is a statement of responsibility plus a definition, not a must/shall, so Mandatory is a judgement call; the row mostly restates duties set by the regulations.

f.title: Ensure compliance with applicable vigilance requirements for product lines outside the policy scope
f.statement: Although these product lines are out of the scope of this policy, vigilance requirements may still apply. As the manufacturer or MAH, it is your responsibility to ensure compliance with the requirements set out within the Act and regulations applicable to your products.
f.applicability: Product lines excluded from the scope of POL-0041: sperm and ova, medical devices, veterinary products, natural health products, cells, tissues and organs, whole blood and blood components, and biocides

rows.quote: Although these product lines are out of the scope, vigilance requirements may still apply. As the manufacturer or MAH, it is your responsibility to ensure compliance with the requirements set out within the act and regulations applicable to your products.
rows.review_note: Review: new row. Missed statement that MAHs stay responsible for vigilance compliance for out-of-scope product lines. Double-check: statement trimmed to the quote; the list of excluded product lines (from the preceding bullets, not in the quote) moved to applicability. Below 90: the quote refers to 'these product lines' without listing them, the level is a judgement call ('it is your responsibility'), and the row only points back to whichever Act and regulations apply.

f.title: Support alternate approaches to the policy with adequate justification
f.statement: Guidance documents are administrative instruments, so flexibility can be applied; however, to be acceptable, alternate approaches to the principles and practices described in this document must be supported by adequate justification.
f.clause: Overview > Note about guidance documents in general

rows.quote: Guidance documents are administrative, not legal, instruments. This means that flexibility can be applied. However, to be acceptable, alternate approaches to the principles and practices described in this document must be supported by adequate justification.
rows.location: Overview > Note about guidance documents in general
rows.review_note: Review: kept. Standard Health Canada 'guidance documents in general' boilerplate, but it is a genuine duty ('must be supported by adequate justification') that applies when departing from the policy and GUI-0102 during GVP inspections. No change. Double-check: confirmed against the quote. Below 90: standard 'guidance documents in general' wording; passive 'must be supported', so the MAH actor is inferred, and the duty only arises when an alternate approach is used.

f.title: Discuss alternate approaches in advance with the relevant program area
f.statement: Alternate approaches should be discussed in advance with the relevant program area to avoid the possible finding that applicable statutory or regulatory requirements have not been met.
f.clause: Overview > Note about guidance documents in general
